consensus_summary: Sanctify means to set apart as holy for God; sanctification is primarily the process (and/or accomplished state) by which believers are made holy—separated from sin, consecrated, and progressively conformed to Christ by the Holy Spirit—with recognized alternatives for positional/definitive status, entire sanctification, cultic consecration, theosis/sacramental grace, and humans sanctifying God’s name.
book_summary: To remove from common status and place under an owner’s claim for an appointed purpose; also, to acknowledge and treat as holy. God sanctifies by claiming; people sanctify God and His Name by honoring Him as holy.
consensus_core_identification: Set apart as holy / make holy, especially the Spirit-wrought moral-spiritual transformation (or status) of believers
book_core_identification: Remove from common status and place under an owner’s claim for a purpose; acknowledge/treat as holy (God claims; people honor God as holy)
boundary_disagreement: Book centers ownership-claim and reverse human sanctifying of God, demoting progressive inward renewal to a mere ‘commonly taught’ view; consensus treats moral transformation/conformity to Christ as primary while listing cultic claim and reverse usage as secondary or root senses.
material_contradiction: None; the claim/set-apart sense is already present in consensus cultic alternatives, so the cores do not mutually exclude, but the book reweights and re-boundaries what counts as the term’s essential identification.
rationale: Both share the lexical set-apart/holy core, so this is not replacement of referent (not DIVERGENT) nor pure novelty. The book preserves that category yet materially narrows and reclassifies by making owner’s claim the definition and treating progressive moral renewal as non-definitional common teaching, altering extension and precision at the boundary.
strongest_objection: Texts such as 1 Thess 4:3–7 and the dominant NT pattern of Spirit-enabled moral holiness make the progressive/transformational sense difficult to exclude from the core identification.
